# Readiness Report

`mxcli report readiness` measures nothing itself. It reads the other reports, sorts
what they found into **blocking**, **risks** and **accepted**, and gives one verdict
by a rule printed on the page and stored in the JSON. A report that was not given,
or could not check, is **not assessed** — never passing.

## Run it

```bash
# usual: report all writes readiness.html with the others, first on the overview
mxcli report all -p app.mpr -o docs/reports --against v1.4.0 --milestone M2 \
  --journeys journeys.jsonl --spans spans.jsonl --junit results.xml \
  --perf-journeys perf.jsonl --perf-spans perf-spans.jsonl
# re-roll from that folder, e.g. after signing items off
mxcli report readiness --dir docs/reports --milestone M2 -o docs/reports/readiness.html
# without a folder: runs the reports that need no input (release, performance not assessed)
mxcli report readiness -p app.mpr -o readiness.html
```

`--milestone` names the milestone being released: its requirements not built in full
are blocking; other milestones' are risks. `--budget-ms` (default 1000) is the server
time a journey step may take before it is a risk.

## The verdict

- **not ready** — an open blocking item. Each names the report it came from: open that
  report for the evidence and the fix.
- **not assessed in full** — nothing blocking was found, but a report that decides a
  blocking question was not given or could not check: no `mx check` for the project's
  Mendix version, no `--against` for the release, `--offline` for vulnerabilities, no
  test results. Supply the input; do not read this as "ready".
- **ready, with risks** / **ready**.

## Accepting and signing off

Accept on the report the item came from — a security finding `fixed`/`accepted`, a
release change or vulnerability `accepted`, a lint finding through a brain decision —
and readiness lists it under Accepted with that note. A blocking item that has no home
there is signed off on this page: `readiness:<key>` (the page prints the key) with
status `signed off` and a note saying who decided and why, in
`readiness-annotations.yaml` in the reports folder (or `--annotations`). A sign-off is
a decision, not a fix: keep the note specific.

## Never skip

The page lists what no model report covers — production load, hosting, backups and a
restore, licences, a penetration test. Those are checks for someone else, every time;
a green verdict says nothing about them.
